RT @ClaudeDevs: Usage limits are up, effective today we're: 

1) Doubling Claude Code's 5-hour limits for Pro, Max, Team and seat-based Ent…

AI has broken my mental model for time estimates. I used to lean on Pareto's 80/20: first 80% of the work takes 20% of the time. 

I think the underlying principle is still true, but both ratio and curve have moved. Getting to "basically works" is nearly instant, sweating every single last detail still takes a decent chunk of time. 

Maybe it's time to switch to 90/10, 95/5, 98/2?

recent_posts.title:
AI has broken my mental model for time estimates. I used to lean on Pareto's 80/20: first 80% of the work takes 20% of the time. 

I think the underlying principle is still true, but both ratio and curve have moved. Getting to "basically works" is nearly instant, sweating every single last detail still takes a decent chunk of time. 

Maybe it's time to switch to 90/10, 95/5, 98/2?
recent_posts.summary: AI coding tools have dramatically shifted the effort distribution in software development. The classic Pareto 80/20 rule (80% of work in 20% of time) no longer holds — AI gets you to a working prototype nearly instantly, but the remaining polish and edge cases still demand significant effort. The author suggests the ratio may now be closer to 90/10, 95/5, or even 98/2.

recent_posts.title:
A small feature drop in Cowork: Live Artifacts! 

Ask Claude to create a dashboard, report, or deck - and whenever you open it, Claude will refetch data from your Connectors to keep all information up to date. Simple idea, super useful in practice.

Get Claude at . Simply tell Claude that you'd like a "live artifact" to get started.
recent_posts.summary: Cowork has released a new feature called Live Artifacts, which allows users to ask Claude to generate dashboards, reports, or decks that automatically refetch data from connected sources each time they are opened, keeping content up to date.

Use with care, brought to you by @dreamofabear
recent_posts.summary: Claude Cowork now supports a 'skip all permissions' option, a highly requested feature for the AI coding tool. The update was notable enough to warrant a dedicated announcement tweet, with a reminder to use the feature carefully.

recent_posts.title:
Hi! I'm here with *another launch*, it just happens to be extremely niche, nerdy, and probably only for a handful of people. 

In the desktop app, Claude Cowork and Code now have a little Bluetooth API for makers & developers, allowing you to build hardware devices that interact with Claude.

I, for instance, built a little desk pet that alerts me whenever Claude is waiting for permission.
recent_posts.summary: Claude's desktop app now includes a Bluetooth API in Claude Cowork and Code, enabling makers and developers to build hardware devices that interact with Claude. As a demo, the author built a desk pet that alerts when Claude is waiting for permission.

Today is a big day! We're launching a ~ new ~ version of Claude Code in the desktop app. It's been redesigned from the ground up for parallel work and is a lot faster.

It's been my main way to use Claude Code for the last few weeks.
recent_posts.summary: Anthropic has launched a redesigned version of Claude Code in the desktop app, rebuilt from the ground up with a focus on parallel work and improved performance speed.

recent_posts.title:
We released Claude Cowork as a research preview 12 weeks ago. Since then, millions of people have made it part of how they work - and hundreds of thousands more are trying it every week. I'm really optimistic about its ability to make people more productive.

Today, we're removing the "preview" label, marking Claude Cowork as generally available - with new enterprise controls for businesses.
recent_posts.summary: Claude Cowork, Anthropic's collaborative AI workspace tool, has graduated from research preview to general availability after 12 weeks. The milestone comes with millions of active users, hundreds of thousands of new weekly users, and new enterprise controls for businesses.
